feedback: For each sorted circuit, confirm or correct the placement and name the deciding feature (the completed loop, the exact break, or the flat cell).
If a single-wire or same-terminal picture is placed in 'lights', prompt the learner to trace for a RETURN path to the other terminal before deciding.
activities.intendedInsight: The judgement is binary — lights or does not — and depends on whether an unbroken loop exists with a working cell. Naming the specific fault for each non-working circuit reinforces that a path break can sit anywhere in the loop, while a flat cell fails for a different reason (no working energy source).
learnerActions: Given a set of clear, unambiguous circuit pictures, decide for each whether the bulb lights and place it in a 'lights' or 'won't light' group.
For each 'won't light' picture, name the fault (gap in a wire, clip on insulation, loose bulb, open switch, both wires on the same terminal, or a flat cell).
Justify at least one judgement by describing the full loop you traced (or the point where the trace stopped).
activities.title: Sort the circuits: lights vs won't light
